standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-NAK, invoked at proof line 4407
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the surjectivity of the endomorphism f' obtained from the displayed identity to bijectivity, which is the contradiction step.

standard_prerequisites.name: An endomorphism of a finite module that becomes an isomorphism after tensoring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-fun, invoked at proof line 4409
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the surjectivity of f' into the statement that f' is an isomorphism, whence the induced map on the tensor product is an isomorphism, contradicting the annihilation of the chosen element.

core_obligations: Assume the contrary and choose witnesses: write the module as a direct sum of finite modules, take an associated prime q of the tensor product whose sum with the extended maximal ideal is the whole ring, and choose an element whose annihilator is exactly q; after modifying the decomposition slightly one may assume the element lies in the first summand tensored with the test module (proof lines 4388-4394).

Use the assumption to produce an identity of endomorphisms: writing the unit as an element of the prime plus a combination of elements of the maximal ideal with coefficients in the ring, and composing with the inclusion and the projection, gives an identity expressing the identity of the first finite module as an element of the prime plus a combination of the elements of the maximal ideal (proof lines 4395-4405).

Conclude by Nakayama and the isomorphism criterion: the prime component is therefore surjective hence an isomorphism, so the induced map on the tensor product is an isomorphism, which contradicts the fact that the chosen element is annihilated by that component (proof lines 4406-4415).
proof_roadmap: Set up the contradiction with witnesses (proof lines 4388-4394).
Produce the identity of endomorphisms from the assumption (proof lines 4395-4405).
Nakayama plus the isomorphism criterion gives the contradiction (proof lines 4406-4415).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a module over a local ring which is a direct sum of finite modules, no associated prime of a tensor product with an arbitrary module can generate the unit ideal together with the extended maximal ideal (statement lines 4378-4386, tag 05IU). The proof is a genuine contradiction argument: one chooses an element whose annihilator is the given associated prime and arranges for it to lie in a single summand, uses the assumption to write the identity of that summand as an element of the prime plus a combination of elements of the maximal ideal, applies Nakayama's lemma to make that first component an isomorphism, and then obtains a contradiction because the element is annihilated. The identity and the Nakayama step are the substance, so the claim is H2.
